units: CTC is presented as a scientific/falsifiable framework claiming sustained open-ended adaptation should exhibit measurable reality-driven changes in adaptive mechanism space.
Ask whether open-ended adaptation can occur without Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1); unlimited novelty with unchanged mechanism space would weaken CTC.
Proposed falsifier: Delta mathcal G=0 while Delta N->infinity for sustained genuinely novel adaptive capabilities.
CTC is too strong if equivalent adaptive expansion occurs independently of environmental information and external reality has no causal contribution.
Compare CTC-active vs Delta mathcal G=0; if fixed topology consistently matches open-ended adaptation, the distinction loses explanatory power.
mathcal G is explicitly stated not directly observable.
Candidate proxies are strategy-space change, architecture modification, and counterfactual reachability under E* rightsquigarrow C_rev.
Weak form requires partial mathcal G_(t+1)/partial Omega_t >0.
Strong form requires Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1) with measurable causal contribution; source says strong version is more ambitious/easier to falsify.
Control permeability, feedback, self-modification, learning-mechanism access and reality constraints; measure novelty, adaptation speed, transfer, mechanism diversity.
CTC-active systems are predicted eventually to outperform systems limited to state/knowledge updates.
CTC does not claim all intelligence needs self-modification, complexity implies openness, self-improvement guarantees open-endedness, or every adaptive system becomes evolutionary.
CTC proposes Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1) as necessary for genuine recursive open-ended adaptation and is disproven by Delta mathcal G=0 with unlimited open-ended adaptation.

Implementation roadmap seeks smallest experimental environment testing whether constraint permeability affects recursive adaptation; source calls it the 'Constraint Transition Condition (CTC)' hypothesis here.
Simulator should isolate CTC as causal variable rather than raw performance, reward, scale, or model size; target is future adaptive capacity under constraint access.
Environment->Constraint Signal E*->Revision Mechanism C_rev->Generator Space mathcal G->Agent; switch closed C_rev(t+1)=f(C_rev(t)) vs active f(C_rev(t),E*_t).
Environment should produce tasks, constraints, failures, unexpected conditions and changing objectives, with predictable and unexpected pressure.
R_t supports prediction/compression/abstraction, but representation updates alone do not satisfy CTC.
E* is environmental information for future adaptation; C_rev determines what/how/which improvements/searches update; mathcal G is reachable adaptive mechanisms and Delta mathcal G is key measurement.
Closed condition expected strong short-term optimization/limited novelty; CTC condition expected slower initial optimization, stronger shift adaptation, increased reachable mechanism space.
Measure performance, adaptation velocity, Delta mathcal G, dependency, and capability after removal.
Weaken CTC if enabled systems fail under change, E* access does not expand mechanisms, gains are explained only by extra information, or effects vanish controlling compute/data/parameters/budget.
Phase 1 toy model for initial evidence; Phase 2 changing/adversarial/hidden benchmark environments; Phase 3 RL/evolutionary/agent systems for generalization.

Strongest envisioned result is greater mechanism discovery, novelty adaptation, reduced dependency and preserved reality access; open adaptation requires environmental access to future modification mechanism.
Operational question E* rightsquigarrow C_rev? If yes source labels adaptive lineage; if no internally generated trajectory.
Positions CTC as proposed structural condition on reality constraints and future adaptive mechanisms, not replacement for existing fields.
Source maps variation-selection-inheritance/environmental feedback to Omega_t->Delta mathcal G and says reality influences future-form distribution.
RL environment->reward->policy update may affect state/knowledge while fixed learning architecture leaves Omega not->Delta mathcal G.
Self-modification Delta C_rev!=0 is separated from reality-coupled C_rev(t+1)=f(C_rev(t),E*_t); source calls difference causal ownership.
CTC adds diagnostic whether reality influences the generator of future novelty; novel outputs are distinguished from novelty-generating mechanisms.
Momentary alignment is distinguished from future correction; source uses E* rightsquigarrow C_rev as deeper corrective-access condition.
Information input is not mechanism transformation; receiving large information can coexist with structural closure.
CTC extends input->state correction to input->controller revision.
CTC applies 'what changes what?' recursively to the mechanism deciding change; relevant source edge E* rightsquigarrow C_rev.
CTC excludes complexity/performance/computation/self-modification/novelty-alone definitions and proposes Omega_t->Delta mathcal G as deeper structural property.
Simulator is intended to compare fixed adaptation, closed self-modification and CTC-active adaptation for measurable long-term advantage.
Environment->E*/Omega->Causal Transition Layer->Adaptive Mechanism Space->Agent->new environment; central measurement Omega_t->Delta mathcal G_(t+1).
Simulator components: environment, observation, constraint extraction, adaptive-mechanism controller, agent execution.
E_t/Omega_t environment has task T_t, hidden structure S_t, perturbations Delta E including rules/objectives/physics/constraints.
Agent layers: state X_t, representation K_t, generator space mathcal G_t, revision mechanism C_rev,t.
Baseline mathcal G fixed; internal C_rev(t+1)=f(C_rev(t)); CTC C_rev(t+1)=f(C_rev(t),E_t), equivalent to Omega->Delta mathcal G.
Each timestep: environment, observation, constraint extraction, CTC evaluation, updates X/K/G/C_rev, environment change; formal E->Omega->C_rev->mathcal G->X->E.
Mode 1 no Omega->Delta mathcal G; Mode 2 internal C_rev self-update; Mode 3 CTC-active Omega->Delta mathcal G.
Proposed P_t capability, A_s=DeltaP/Delta t, M_e=|Delta mathcal G|, transfer P_new/P_old, dependency D->0.
Closed systems may match/beat short term; CTC systems should outperform long term due to reality reshaping future adaptation.
Proposed first prototype files: environment.py, agent.py, mechanism_space.py, ctc_controller.py, metrics.py, experiment.py.
Open-ended intelligence is proposed to require reality access to future-adaptation mechanism; test asks whether world influences what future change becomes possible.

Fixed adaptation: reality/input/system updates state/better performance but adaptation stays inside fixed possibility space; recursive adaptation: reality/constraint/system updates itself/new mechanisms and possibility space changes.
Text diagram gives Omega_t -> Delta mathcal G_(t+1) and states mechanism of adaptation changes.
Difference is not whether both systems change, but whether information from reality can change the mechanism generating future changes; CTC marks transition.
